items.basis: The proposed mechanism addresses corrosion detection and repair but fails to address the actual problem: biofilm and scale accumulation. The candidate conflates corrosion with fouling, which are distinct failure modes with different mechanisms and solutions.

The boundary conditions specify a stainless steel plate heat exchanger in a district cooling loop, but the candidate provides no evidence that microcapsule-based self-healing agents can function effectively in the complex thermal cycling and varying flow conditions of such a system.

The provided evidence bundle contains studies on bimetallic steels, atmospheric corrosion of 304 stainless steel, concrete cracking, and welding techniques for magnesium alloys—none of which support the feasibility of fiber optic sensing combined with microcapsule-based self-healing for heat exchanger fouling prevention.

The candidate claims a 300% lifespan extension and 70% maintenance cost reduction but provides no comparative analysis against the baseline performance of standard cleaning protocols or alternative anti-fouling treatments, making these claims unsubstantiated.

Embedding microstructured optical fiber sensors and microcapsules throughout stainless steel heat exchanger plates would compromise the structural integrity and thermal performance of the heat exchanger, creating new failure points and reducing heat transfer efficiency.

The testable prediction focuses on healing agent depletion and repair effectiveness but fails to define how it will measure the critical parameters of heat transfer coefficient and pressure drop reduction—the actual metrics that determine the solution's success.
